eps.o: When the shop's eccentric owner drops by, the staff walks him through their daily routines while he wonders whether to keep the place open or sell it.
After a secret fling with Julia's mom, Luke flexes his fatherly side with a party of drama students who makes things difficult for Julia and the crew.
A couple's public break-up at the restaurant sparks a gender divide among the staff with the guys and the girls taking different sides.
Ryan plans a special surprise for Grace's birthday involving a giant cake, while Luke, Tommy and Julia lock themselves on the roof.
While Aidan stresses over hair loss, a new "no phones" policy at the pizzeria forces the staff into helping Tommy confront his girlfriend.
The staff finds a stack of lottery tickets and imagines how their lives could change. Their big dreams spiral into chaos — but result in a hot tub.
Ryan tries to put the finishing touches on his college application essay while a troop of young scouts takes over the pizza place for the day.
The crew struggles when Mr. Sylvester requires them to sing and dance to provide a better customer experience.
Julia convinces the crew to come over for a sleepover at her house, but the night doesn't go smoothly — especially with a pet spider on the loose.
Hyde joins forces with Julia to track down the pizza shop's notorious prank caller, and Tommy goes around with an odd request to pass a test.
A new female employee creates a rift between the girls and the guys, leading the boys to lean heavily into their masculinity like never before.
When Mr. Sylvester needs the staff to shoot a TV commercial, Tommy takes the director's chair and Luke gets ready for his breakout role.
Aidan searches for a nickname while the rest of the staff gathers evidence after witnessing what they think is an affair between two of their teachers.
The crew must decide who will work on New Year's Eve. During the holiday shift, Tommy has relationship trouble, and Julia tries to get her first kiss.
